title: fix(app-shell): Studio's field type catalog gains the spec's user, secret and record types (objectui#11909)
body:
Fixes #11909

Clause-②: no (measured: no declaration reachable from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s entry typings imports the catalog; a walk of the built `dist/index.d.ts` import graph reaches 160 typings files and none of `field-types`, `FieldTypePicker`, `ObjectFormCanvas`, `ObjectFieldInspector`, `FieldStub` or `object-fields-io`).

## What changed

Studio's field type catalog, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/field-types.ts`, now holds every member of the installed spec's `FieldType`. It gains the three it lacked:

| type | category | icon | name, en / zh |
|---|---|---|---|
| `secret` | Text, beside `password` | `KeyRound` | Secret / 密钥 |
| `user` | Relation, beside `lookup` and `tree` | `User` | User / 用户 |
| `record` | Advanced, beside `composite` and `repeater` | `Braces` | Record Map / 命名分组 |

- `FieldTypeId` is now the spec's own `FieldType` (a type-only import from `@objectstack/spec/data`). `FIELD_TYPE_META` is a total `Record` over it, so it fails type-check while it lacks a spec member.
- Name and description rows, en and zh, sit beside their siblings in the designer's table, `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`.
- The header's stale count ("46 entries as of spec 7.1") is gone. Per AGENTS.md #9 the header now points at the parity pin instead of writing a number. It also lists what a new entry needs. The old "adding a type here is enough" missed the i18n rows.
- Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch.

The categories follow the spec's own grouping comments in `FieldType`:
- `secret` is declared under "Core Text", next to `password`.
- `user` is "a lookup specialized to the `sys_user` system object".
- `record` is the third embedded structured value, with `composite` and `repeater`.

## Premise check (base `f1781be3a`, installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0)

- **H1, holds.** The spec's `FieldType.options` holds every catalog id, plus `secret`, `user` and `record`. The catalog had no id the spec lacks, so there was nothing extra to report or remove.
- **H2, holds, with no config key to add.** The spec fixes `user`'s target as a constant of the type: `referenceTargetOf` in the spec's field-value module says metadata "authored without it ... is fully specified". `secret`'s masking comes from the spec's `MASKED_ON_READ_FIELD_TYPES` table, not from a field key. So adding a field of each type writes `{ type, label }` and nothing else. No key is invented. `FieldSchema`, `ObjectSchema` and `assertObjectMetadataWritable` all accept it.
- **H3, holds.** The Type control resolves the showcase's `user`, `secret` and `record` fields to their entries.
- **H4, holds.** The parity pin reads `FieldType.options` when it runs. It is a unit test, not a script, workflow or gate.

## Tests

Two new files sit beside the catalog.

`field-types.spec-parity-11909.test.ts` (unit) pins:
- parity in both directions against the installed enum;
- each entry keyed by its own id;
- the pickers offer every spec type exactly once;
- a name row and a description row in both tables for every spec type;
- the three ids resolve to their own entries, with the unknown-type fallback as a lit control.

`field-types.studioSurfaces-11909.test.tsx` (dom) covers the real `ObjectFieldInspector` and the real `ObjectFormCanvas`:
- **Type control, reading.** The inspector reads each of the showcase's five fields by its type's name in en, and `f_user` in zh, with no "(not found)". The fields are built with the spec's `Field.user` and `Field.secret` builders, and with the showcase's literal for `record`. A `legacy_widget` lit control still reads flagged.
- **Type control, choosing.** It offers all three types, and choosing User writes `{ type: 'user', label }`.
- **Add-field palette.** It adds each type with a body that `FieldSchema`, `ObjectSchema` and `assertObjectMetadataWritable` accept.

All runs below are at HEAD `c174e7721`, from the repo root, under the verify lock on a shared box.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over 33 files: `Test Files  33 passed (33)`, `Tests  500 passed (500)`. The 33 files are:
  - the two new files;
  - the objectui#11793 Type picker test, the one existing importer of `field-types`;
  - every app-shell test that names a consumer of the catalog: `ObjectFormCanvas`, `ObjectFieldInspector`, `FieldTypePicker`, `ViewColumnPanes` or `FieldStub`;
  - `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exits 0 on both legs, `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`. The dependency closure was built first.

### Ablations

Each ablation ran from committed HEAD. The mutation went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proves the anchor hit and the blob changed. It then restored the file and proved the blob equals HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

- **A: the catalog loses its `user` row.** 9 failed, 10 passed across the two files. Parity names `[ 'user' ]`, and every `user` case of the inspector and the canvas goes red. The `secret` and `record` cases stay green.
- **B: the en table loses `engine.fieldType.user`.** Only the rows pin goes red, naming `en-US engine.fieldType.user`. The DOM file stays green, and that is why the rows pin exists: `t()` returns the key itself, so a rendered name compared against `t()` cannot tell a real name from a missing one.
- **C: the catalog gains a `legacy_widget` the spec lacks.** 3 failed, 4 passed. The reverse-direction pin names `[ 'legacy_widget' ]`. My first two attempts at C were refused by the tool before any test ran, because the replacement text contained the anchor. They measured nothing and are not counted.
- **D: the `user` row removed, checked by `tsc --noEmit -p packages/app-shell/tsconfig.json`.** Exit 2, with TS2741 "Property 'user' is missing" on `FIELD_TYPE_META`.

## Gates

Each exit code was captured before any pipe.

- Green, each exit 0, with these verdict lines:
  - `check:i18n-designer-parity`: "Every en row has a zh row, and every shared row carries the same placeholders."
  - `check:i18n-drift`: 6 designer keys added, 0 en values changed.
  - `check:i18n-keys`
  - `check:spec-symbols`
  - `check:new-line-citations`: "0 new citation(s)".
  - `check:control-bytes`
  - `check:icon-record-names`
  - `check:designer-field-key-parity`
  - `check:phantom-deps`
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` and `check:vi-mock-override-shape`
  - `check:test-path-roots`
  - `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`
  - `check:metadata-write-doors`
  - `check:unreferenced-sources`
  - `check:eager-closure`, see below
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: 1 changeset declared for 4 released source files.
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`
  - `pnpm exec eslint` on the four touched source and test files.
- `check:spec-floors`, with app-shell built: app-shell is not among the findings, so its spec references were judged clean against its `^17.6.0` floor. The gate still exits 1, on four `[no-artifact]` findings for `cli`, `plugin-gantt`, `plugin-timeline` and `plugin-tree`. This diff touches none of them and they were not built here: NOT MEASURED for those four.

## Eager closure (asked for by the seat; objectui#11937 owns the main-red)

Both builds were `vite build` of `apps/console`, under the lock, followed by `pnpm check:eager-closure`. The base build used the same worktree with the two source files this diff changes checked out at `f1781be3a`. Those are the only non-test `src` paths the diff touches. They were then restored, with blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| | eager closure, gzip | raw | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `f1781be3a` | 3,385,951 B (3306.6 KB) | 11,477,791 B | green, headroom 0.4 KB |
| head `c174e7721` | 3,386,275 B (3306.9 KB) | 11,478,833 B | green, headroom 0.1 KB |
| delta | **+324 B** | +1,042 B | 336 of 2458 chunks are eager in both builds |

The chunks that moved:
- `i18n`, the metadata-admin designer table: +227 B gzip, +758 B raw. These are the 12 new rows.
- `ReportDefaultInspector`, the chunk that carries the catalog: +97 B gzip, +284 B raw.
- Seven other chunks moved by 1 to 5 B gzip with 0 B raw. That is hash churn in import specifiers.
- `ui-components` is unchanged, because the three icons were already in it.

Both readings are green against this base. `main` `19a7348` is already red on Bundle Analysis (objectui#11937), so this PR's Bundle Analysis is expected red until that lands.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs-driven (AGENTS.md #2).** No README or `content/docs` sentence names the catalog's types or its count, so there is nothing to report. The queries were `git grep` over `*.md`, `*.mdx`, `content/**` and the package READMEs, for "46 entries", "N field types", "field type catalog", `FIELD_TYPE_META`, `TYPES_BY_CATEGORY` and Studio "field type" plus picker or palette wording.
- **Out of scope: the record default editor (reported to the seat, not touched here).** The inspector offers a text "Default value" control on a `record` field. `defaultValueKind` in `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` lists `composite` and `repeater` as having no default, but not `record`. Any value committed there is refused by `FieldSchema`. I measured this through the real inspector in a one-shot probe (not committed):
  - `{ type: 'record', label: 'F', defaultValue: 'primary' }` fails to parse with "the default \"primary\" cannot satisfy this field's own stored value contract".
  - `composite` renders no control.
  - `text` renders one, and its value parses.
  - The showcase's `f_record` already showed this control before this PR. This PR also makes `record` addable from the palette.
- **Noted, not filed.** `FieldStub` draws the three types with its generic input and their raw type id as a badge on the canvas preview. That is cosmetic. `secret` and `user` take the inspector's free-text default control, and the spec accepts what it writes.
